barricade.worldRole: A temporary, deliberately understandable interruption in the enemy route that turns path control into a visible player-authored hypothesis.
barricade.manufactureContext: Built rapidly in the fortress workshop from standardized structural modules intended to be repaired, replaced and visibly tested under pressure.
barricade.emotionalIntent: Dependable and brave without appearing invulnerable; its damage should create urgency and useful concern rather than helplessness.
barricade.oneSecondPromise: This broad grounded object blocks a lane now, shows where it is weakening, and can be understood before the next enemy reaches it.
barricade.orientationCue: The reinforced presentation face addresses incoming enemies; the flatter service face and interaction light address the player.
barricade.interactionCue: A complete, waist-height service socket or status module is readable from the safe rear side.
barricade.dangerCue: Breaks, tilted panels and exposed structure progress from one localized weakness to a wide critical breach.
barricade.relationToPlayer: Friendly player-built infrastructure that invites repair and repositioning rather than fear.
proportionRules: The full width remains exactly twice the height and four times the depth.
The two feet occupy the outer thirds and keep a clear central ground gap.
The blocking panels occupy most of the frontal area while the frame remains the silhouette authority.
The interaction module stays above the player's ground clutter and below the top rail.

viewDescriptions.front: A wide low fortress gate fragment: two planted feet, two outer posts, strong top and bottom rails, and three readable blocking bays facing the enemy.
viewDescriptions.back: A calmer service plane with visible frame continuity, repair access and the interaction module; it must never resemble the enemy-facing impact side.
viewDescriptions.left: A compact planted wedge showing the foot depth, post thickness and credible connection between panel, rail and ground contact.
viewDescriptions.right: The mirrored functional profile with only approved territory asymmetry; no cable, plate or damage fragment may float outside the structural chain.
viewDescriptions.top: A shallow defensive bar with two stable footprints and a clear front-to-back distinction created by impact armor versus service mass.
viewDescriptions.bottom: Only grounded feet, underslung rail structure and intentional clearances are visible; no decorative underside detail consumes budget.
viewDescriptions.threeQuarterFront: The canonical hero read combines broad blocking silhouette, panel rhythm, planted feet and the enemy-facing reinforcement logic.
viewDescriptions.threeQuarterBack: The service read exposes repair logic and interaction access while preserving the same outer silhouette and footprint.
viewDescriptions.gameCamera: From elevated third-person mobile view, the object reads as one broad lane blocker with three state-readable bays, not as a pile of small parts.

objective_core.worldRole: The fortress heart, battle objective and persistent visual anchor that converts abstract survival into protection of a player-authored home.
objective_core.manufactureContext: A deliberately overbuilt energy core assembled as the center of the fortress. Approved service and replacement motifs may suggest maintenance history without claiming a persistent history system.
objective_core.emotionalIntent: Precious, resilient and worth rallying around; damage should feel alarming but legible, never arbitrary or hopeless.
objective_core.oneSecondPromise: This tall protected glowing heart is the thing the fortress exists to defend, and its current health can be read from across the battlefield.
objective_core.orientationCue: The brighter interaction aperture and protective opening face the player approach; the denser service mass closes the rear.
objective_core.interactionCue: A complete protected ring and accessible lower service band identify friendly interaction without resembling a weapon.
objective_core.dangerCue: Protective rings open, buttresses fail and the core becomes more exposed as health worsens.
objective_core.relationToPlayer: Friendly shared home anchor whose survival expresses group competence and persistent identity.
proportionRules: The protected luminous core occupies the central third of total height.

viewDescriptions.bottom: A broad load-distributing base and service conduits remain simple, grounded and free of decorative clutter.

viewDescriptions.threeQuarterBack: The service spine and denser rear protection explain construction without hiding the core state.

enemy_standard.worldRole: The readable standard zombie of the horde: a fair baseline pressure unit that lets players judge route, damage and defensive choices without borrowing the wall-breaking silhouette of a brute.
enemy_standard.manufactureContext: A stylized undead body transformed by one stable violet frontier mutation. Biology is always primary; sparse hardened growth expresses a fixed hostile condition without implying adaptive learning, player-built armor, copper repair authorship or mechanical chassis language.
enemy_standard.emotionalIntent: Immediately recognizable as a zombie, lightly unsettling and tenacious with a touch of awkward physical absurdity, but never realistic, graphic, tragic or gore-dependent.
enemy_standard.technologyLevel: undead biological threat with hardened frontier growth
enemy_standard.oneSecondPromise: A hunched violet zombie with a visible face, reaching unequal arms and a broken-crown shoulder bloom advances toward the fortress and shows weakening through posture before color.
enemy_standard.orientationCue: The bowed zombie head, dark face cavity, forward jaw and reaching arm lead the hunched body; the violet bloom sweeps from one side of the crown toward the opposite shoulder and never reads as a visor.
enemy_standard.interactionCue: No friendly socket, complete ring, service panel or repair affordance exists; the face and hands are target cues, not interaction controls.
enemy_standard.dangerCue: A forward cranial profile, open reaching hands, bent pursuit posture and a short pre-swipe draw-back communicate attack intent without giant fists or weapon props.
enemy_standard.relationToPlayer: A hostile but fair baseline zombie whose facing, swipe preparation, stagger and collapse support immediate recognition, causal combat reading and honest post-failure understanding.
proportionRules: The hunched pear-shaped torso occupies roughly forty-two percent of total height and remains narrower than a brute.
The cranial mass occupies sixteen to twenty percent of total height and projects forward by roughly fifteen percent of body depth.
Arms are thick enough for horde readability but hands remain medium, open and smaller than the head so the unit never promises wall-breaking force.
Bent legs occupy roughly one third of total height and preserve a clear gap between the feet at mobile distance.
The asymmetrical violet bloom stays inside the two-and-a-half-stud width and cannot become a horn, backpack, armor plate or second head.

viewDescriptions.front: A clearly undead violet rôdeur with a bowed visible head, dark expressive face cavity, hunched pear torso, unequal reaching arms and bent separated legs.
viewDescriptions.back: A continuous biological back and one oblique hardened violet bloom reveal the same hunched anatomy without service boxes, armor chassis or invented machinery.
viewDescriptions.left: The forward skull, jaw, rounded upper back and one lower dragging forearm create an unmistakable shambling zombie profile.
viewDescriptions.right: The counter-profile preserves the head-led hunch while the shorter reaching arm and shoulder bloom explain controlled asymmetry.
viewDescriptions.top: The head, hunched spine and hands form a compact forward arrow through pose, while the body itself remains rounded and biological rather than wedge-armored.
viewDescriptions.bottom: Two broad simplified feet, bent ankle connections and a stable animation footprint remain readable and compatible with the feet-center pivot.
viewDescriptions.threeQuarterFront: The canonical read combines visible zombie face, forward cranial hood, hunched violet body, one reaching hand, one lower dragging hand and the oblique shoulder bloom.
viewDescriptions.threeQuarterBack: The rounded spine, asymmetric bloom path, bent legs and hanging arms remain anatomically compatible with the front view and contain no mechanical invention.
viewDescriptions.gameCamera: At horde scale the unit reads as one purple shambling zombie token: head-led, hunched, open-handed and visibly stateful without surface noise.

giant fists, wall-breaking shoulders or heroic combat stance
gore, exposed tissue, detached anatomy or realistic decay
random crystals, horns, backpack growth or second head

floor_module.visualThesis: A precise fortress grid cell whose single approved replacement quadrant records maintenance while every edge key, footprint and construction rhythm stays exact.
floor_module.constructionTranslation: A calm square chassis, large inset and thick edge keys provide tile readability; only one quadrant or connector receives a copper-bounded replacement treatment.
signatureDetails: one grouped fastener cluster at the real joint
floor_module.stateTranslation: The known replacement seam carries the only approved damage read while the grid cell remains a reliable construction surface.

stateTranslations.intact: The square grid cell is flat, locked and continuous; one copper-bounded replacement quadrant records approved maintenance without implying present failure.
stateTranslations.damaged: The known replacement seam lifts slightly and one edge key opens as a visual-only damage cue; the tile remains flat enough to promise unchanged movement, placement and collision.

artDirectionOverrides.asymmetry: One replacement quadrant and its real fastener cluster provide the only asymmetry; square footprint, edge keys, height, tiling rhythm, movement plane and placement promise remain exact.

damage_effect.visualThesis: A forceful graphic impact sentence whose large vector wedge, bent arc and two or three material-matched fragments preserve target visibility and frontier tactility.
damage_effect.constructionTranslation: The effect inherits Industrial-level shape economy and direction clarity, then expresses Salvaged Frontier through material-matched fragments, warm edge sparks and restrained dusty weight.
signatureDetails: two or three material-matched heavy fragments
damage_effect.stateTranslation: Severity changes only the scale and break rhythm of one fixed impact vector; the target, direction and cause remain unobscured.

stateTranslations.damaged: One compact vector wedge, one continuous bent arc and two or three target-matched fragments identify a meaningful hit while preserving target silhouette and lane visibility.
stateTranslations.critical: The same vector expands, the primary arc breaks once and one fragment becomes larger; density stays bounded and the effect never resembles a persistent object or a second gameplay state.

artDirectionOverrides.thesis: A transient Salvaged Frontier impact sentence communicates target, direction, severity and cause through one graphic vector, material-matched fragments and restrained dusty weight without becoming physical scenery.
shapeGrammar: one dominant directional wedge
one bent or broken secondary arc
two or three large target-matched fragments
one clean negative-space corridor around the target
artDirectionOverrides.exaggeration: Direction and severity are enlarged enough to read for a fraction of a second on mobile, while fragment count, spark density and total screen coverage remain strictly bounded.
artDirectionOverrides.edgeLanguage: The main vector uses one clean graphic edge and the fragments inherit the target material; no structural bevel language, chassis outline or persistent solid frame is allowed.
artDirectionOverrides.detailDensity: One primary vector, one secondary arc and at most three readable fragments carry the effect; micro-particles and decorative debris are forbidden.
artDirectionOverrides.asymmetry: Asymmetry follows the impact direction and target normal only; the same vector topology must remain consistent across diagnostic views of one generated state.
artDirectionOverrides.materialLanguage: Fragments briefly inherit the struck material, warm copper-gold edges indicate force and a restrained dust body adds frontier tactility; the effect owns no chassis material system.
artDirectionOverrides.paletteLogic: Target-matched fragments and a bounded warm force accent carry meaning; mint interaction, permanent player-construction colors and broad critical red fields are forbidden.
artDirectionOverrides.surfaceTreatment: Use crisp vector readability, broad translucent dust and a few solid fragments with no painted lighting, texture chatter, smoke cloud or cinematic bloom.
artDirectionOverrides.wearLogic: The effect has no persistent wear history; severity changes the same impact sentence and disappears without leaving invented geometry or undocumented damage.
forbidden: physical chassis, pedestal, brace, panel, foot or service socket
persistent prop, debris pile or environmental object reading
screen-filling smoke, bloom or particle noise
more than three readable solid fragments
hidden target, hidden lane or ambiguous impact direction
invented text, icon, emblem or user-interface graphic

turret_fast_v1.visualThesis: A fast twin-barrel turret built on a calm planted chassis, with one adapted firing housing and one repaired rear service pack making speed, ownership and history immediately legible.
turret_fast_v1.constructionTranslation: The pedestal, body, barrel spacing, protected yokes and safe-side socket use thick modular discipline; one compatible housing, one large reinforcement and one copper repair band create the authored asymmetry.
signatureDetails: one adapted but equally readable barrel housing
one offset rear service pack with a protected mint socket
turret_fast_v1.stateTranslation: The adapted firing side carries the full visual damage progression while foundation, facing, anchors and service orientation remain fixed.

stateTranslations.intact: Both barrels share a clear forward aim and the adapted housing remains visibly integrated; the turret reads as visually ready without claiming an implemented targeting or firing contract.
stateTranslations.damaged: The adapted-side barrel drops at its visible pivot, its guard opens and the remaining barrel holds a plausible ready posture; visual readiness never proves actual tracking or firing capability.
stateTranslations.critical: The same barrel is absent, the upper mass rests in a disabled tilt and the rear socket opens along the existing repair chain; no runtime capability change is claimed until the defense gameplay contract is accepted.

artDirectionOverrides.asymmetry: One adapted barrel housing, one real load-bearing reinforcement and one offset rear service pack create controlled authorship; pedestal, aim axis, barrel spacing, anchors, footprint and safe-side interaction remain fixed.

clean-tactical-diorama.thesis: A pristine tactical model of a living fortress: disciplined geometry, semantic color fields and near-perfect modular order make cause, function and state exceptionally legible.
shapeGrammar: precise rectangles, trapezoids and approved radial forms
clean chamfers and planar cuts
strict modular alignment
semantic panels with zero decorative noise
clean-tactical-diorama.exaggeration: Proportions are selectively amplified for function and state, but construction remains calm, measured and almost diagrammatic.
clean-tactical-diorama.edgeLanguage: Consistent medium chamfers create clean readable bands with no accidental soft sculpting.
clean-tactical-diorama.detailDensity: Minimal tertiary detail; seams, apertures and connectors appear only where they clarify a system.
clean-tactical-diorama.asymmetry: Two-percent near-perfect symmetry, broken only by the required service orientation or state damage.
clean-tactical-diorama.materialLanguage: Clean matte structural fields, controlled functional metal and precisely bounded semantic inserts.
clean-tactical-diorama.paletteLogic: Large quiet value groups carry identity; small semantic fields carry interaction, warning, critical and threat roles.
clean-tactical-diorama.surfaceTreatment: No random wear, noise or dirt; approved damage and repair are graphic, local and causal.
clean-tactical-diorama.wearLogic: Intact assets are nearly pristine; state damage creates exact exposed planes and broken modules rather than surface grime.
forbidden: uncontrolled texture noise
decorative panel line spam
organic dents
unapproved asymmetry
material gradients that hide semantic boundaries

barricade.visualThesis: A tactical lane-control glyph made physical: three exact panels, a continuous dark frame and one precise rear interaction field.
barricade.constructionTranslation: Every module aligns to a measured grid; joints are clean cuts, not toy brackets or salvage patches.
barricade.stateTranslation: Damage creates one exact missing panel corner, then a large clean breach with graphic critical exposure.

objective_core.visualThesis: A pristine tactical objective marker embodied as a protected luminous core inside disciplined radial geometry.
objective_core.constructionTranslation: Symmetric buttresses, exact ring spacing and a clean access notch turn the objective into a three-dimensional diagram.
objective_core.stateTranslation: Protection sectors open in clean measured steps; critical exposure is graphic and unmistakable.

enemy_standard.visualThesis: A clean violet zombie threat token whose bowed face, hunched pear torso, unequal open hands and bent legs remain separable from every other horde role.
enemy_standard.constructionTranslation: Exact broad anatomical masses and one controlled crown-to-shoulder bloom preserve horde clarity; no mechanical joints, armor chassis or giant fists are introduced.
enemy_standard.materialTranslation: Render deep violet matte biology, one calmer mid-violet bloom and a tiny raspberry face focus as flat tactical material groups. No copper, mint, bone panels, metal shell or realistic flesh detail.
enemy_standard.stateTranslation: Damage lowers one shoulder and opens the fixed bloom fracture; critical state buckles one knee and trails the same arm while preserving exact identity and footprint.

floor_module.visualThesis: A pristine tactical grid cell with a large inset, exact edge keys and almost no visual noise.
floor_module.constructionTranslation: Every seam is aligned, every connector is repeated and the top view reads like a clean construction diagram.
floor_module.stateTranslation: One clean corner displacement or missing connector creates the entire damaged read.

damage_effect.visualThesis: A graphic tactical impact glyph: exact vector wedge, clean arc and limited fragments communicate cause faster than spectacle.
damage_effect.constructionTranslation: The effect uses flat readable shapes, bounded emission and strict timing like a spatial interface element.
damage_effect.stateTranslation: Critical severity increases scale and break structure while keeping the effect diagrammatically clear.

turret_fast_v1.visualThesis: A precise twin-barrel tactical defense token with measured clearances, symmetric supports and one bounded safe-side interaction field.
turret_fast_v1.constructionTranslation: Foundation, pedestal, body, yokes and service mass align to a strict modular grid with zero decorative excess.
turret_fast_v1.stateTranslation: One barrel drops by an approved angle; critical state removes it and tilts the upper module in one clean readable step.
